{
  "hook": "Ramnista grows Xinomavro on Naoussa's steep, iron-rich slopes at 350 meters, where the 100% varietal rule forces focus on this grape's Nebbiolo-like traits. Kir Yianni ages it in French oak to balance the site's firm tannins with red fruit core. This delivers a structured red that punches above Greece's price norms.",
  "wine_summary": "Kir Yianni sources Ramnista from its own hillside estate in Naoussa, where Xinomavro must comprise 100% of reds per appellation rules. The producer stands out for modernizing Naoussa's traditional style, planting at higher elevations for better acidity retention amid warming climates. These choices yield wines with brighter fruit and aging grip compared to lower-altitude Naoussa peers.",
  "terroir_expression": "Naoussa's phyllite and schist soils—crumbled from ancient metamorphic rock—drain fast and impart mineral tension to Xinomavro, translating to graphite-edged red cherry in the glass. Continental climate with cold winters and dry summers, moderated by Vermio Mountain breezes, preserves acidity against the grape's natural rusticity, yielding paler reds with persistent structure over plushness.",
  "vinification_summary": "Kir Yianni ferments Ramnista in temperature-controlled stainless steel, then ages 12-18 months in French barriques to soften Xinomavro's aggressive tannins without masking terroir. *Malolactic fermentation* follows, converting sharp malic acid to softer lactic for rounder mouthfeel. These steps tame the grape's volatility while highlighting site-driven fruit purity.",
  "food_pairing": "Pair with Nashville hot chicken: spice cuts through Xinomavro's tannins, acidity matches vinegar tang. Grilled octopus skewers work for casual bites—charred smokiness echoes the wine's mineral schist notes. Fine dining: lamb shank braised in rosemary—fat yields to the structure, herbs lift red fruit. Tomato-based moussaka balances acidity with the wine's cherry core. Pork souvlaki skewers: char and lemon amplify the palate's ferrous edge.",
  "comparable_wines": "Langhe Nebbiolo from Vietti — shares Xinomavro's tart cherry and alpine tannin grip from similar cool-climate slopes. Barolo Riserva from Giacomo Conterno — matches aging potential and soil-driven minerality at higher price. Naoussa 'Kitsiki' from Kir-Yianni — same producer's younger vine version with softer entry.",
  "style_profile": "Xinomavro medium-body red with grippy tannins and ferrous cherry depth",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2015 and 2013 now through 2028; earlier vintages peaked. Store at 55°F in humid dark conditions to preserve color and fruit.",
  "value_assessment": "$29 at Spec's beats entry Nebbiolo from Piedmont, which hits $35+ for similar structure. Underprices Tuscan Sangiovese like Fontodi's at $40 with less aging upside. Worth buying for Xinomavro fans—medals across vintages confirm consistency.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers list it on Greek or 'next Nebbiolo' sections for curious diners seeking value alternatives to Italy. Retail targets collectors building cellars under $30 who track TEXSOM medals. Casual drinkers discover it via awards-driven shelves.",
  "insider_take": "Skip if you demand instant plushness—Xinomavro's slow evolution frustrates ripe red chasers. But it crushes Barolo wannabes at one-fifth the cost for patient palates. Buy multiples of 2015; it's the vintage that rewires skeptics on Greek reds.",
  "aging_potential_years": 10,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 5,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 12,

    "color_intensity": "medium",

  }
}

parsed.hook: Ramnista grows Xinomavro on Naoussa's steep, iron-rich slopes at 350 meters, where the 100% varietal rule forces focus on this grape's Nebbiolo-like traits. Kir Yianni ages it in French oak to balance the site's firm tannins with red fruit core. This delivers a structured red that punches above Greece's price norms.
parsed.wine_summary: Kir Yianni sources Ramnista from its own hillside estate in Naoussa, where Xinomavro must comprise 100% of reds per appellation rules. The producer stands out for modernizing Naoussa's traditional style, planting at higher elevations for better acidity retention amid warming climates. These choices yield wines with brighter fruit and aging grip compared to lower-altitude Naoussa peers.
parsed.terroir_expression: Naoussa's phyllite and schist soils—crumbled from ancient metamorphic rock—drain fast and impart mineral tension to Xinomavro, translating to graphite-edged red cherry in the glass. Continental climate with cold winters and dry summers, moderated by Vermio Mountain breezes, preserves acidity against the grape's natural rusticity, yielding paler reds with persistent structure over plushness.
parsed.vinification_summary: Kir Yianni ferments Ramnista in temperature-controlled stainless steel, then ages 12-18 months in French barriques to soften Xinomavro's aggressive tannins without masking terroir. *Malolactic fermentation* follows, converting sharp malic acid to softer lactic for rounder mouthfeel. These steps tame the grape's volatility while highlighting site-driven fruit purity.
parsed.food_pairing: Pair with Nashville hot chicken: spice cuts through Xinomavro's tannins, acidity matches vinegar tang. Grilled octopus skewers work for casual bites—charred smokiness echoes the wine's mineral schist notes. Fine dining: lamb shank braised in rosemary—fat yields to the structure, herbs lift red fruit. Tomato-based moussaka balances acidity with the wine's cherry core. Pork souvlaki skewers: char and lemon amplify the palate's ferrous edge.
parsed.comparable_wines: Langhe Nebbiolo from Vietti — shares Xinomavro's tart cherry and alpine tannin grip from similar cool-climate slopes. Barolo Riserva from Giacomo Conterno — matches aging potential and soil-driven minerality at higher price. Naoussa 'Kitsiki' from Kir-Yianni — same producer's younger vine version with softer entry.
parsed.style_profile: Xinomavro medium-body red with grippy tannins and ferrous cherry depth
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink 2015 and 2013 now through 2028; earlier vintages peaked. Store at 55°F in humid dark conditions to preserve color and fruit.
parsed.value_assessment: $29 at Spec's beats entry Nebbiolo from Piedmont, which hits $35+ for similar structure. Underprices Tuscan Sangiovese like Fontodi's at $40 with less aging upside. Worth buying for Xinomavro fans—medals across vintages confirm consistency.
parsed.market_position: Sommeliers list it on Greek or 'next Nebbiolo' sections for curious diners seeking value alternatives to Italy. Retail targets collectors building cellars under $30 who track TEXSOM medals. Casual drinkers discover it via awards-driven shelves.
parsed.insider_take: Skip if you demand instant plushness—Xinomavro's slow evolution frustrates ripe red chasers. But it crushes Barolo wannabes at one-fifth the cost for patient palates. Buy multiples of 2015; it's the vintage that rewires skeptics on Greek reds.
